facts.text: Tanaina’s name comes from the Dena'ina people, whose culture stresses respect for land and sustainable subsistence, a legacy still felt today.
The area features pitted outwash plains and morainic deposits, with local relief of 100 to 200 feet amid rugged mountains like the Talkeetna range.
Winter temperatures in Tanaina range from 10°F to 20°F, with January highs around 24°F and lows near 11°F, according to nearby Palmer data.
Tanaina lies just four miles north of Wasilla, placing it within the Anchorage metropolitan statistical area.
The community sits at 61°37′27″N 149°25′58″W, a precise point that marks its position on the map.
Tanaina’s terrain rolls through boreal forests, with the Chugach Mountains to the south and the Alaska Range to the north shaping its landscape.
